attributes.body_ja:
「際（さい）」は特定（とくてい）の時点（じてん）を表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。この名詞（めいし）に助詞（じょし）の「に」が付（つ）いた「際（さい）に」は、「(A) のときに」「(A) の機会（きかい）に」「(A) の場合（ばあい）」というような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。文型（ぶんけい）としては硬（かた）く、よくある出来事（できごと）よりも、特別（とくべつ）で重要（じゅうよう）な出来事（できごと）について使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

「際（さい）に」は辞書形（じしょけい）もしくは過去形（かこけい）の動詞（どうし）、または「の」を伴（ともな）う名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に続（つづ）きます。

(A) には一時的（いちじてき）または単発（たんぱつ）の出来事（できごと）が入（はい）ることが多（おお）いですが、必（かなら）ずしもそれだけとは限（かぎ）りません。日常的（にちじょうてき）に起（お）こる出来事（できごと）が入（はい）ることもあります。ただし、その場合（ばあい）、その出来事（できごと）に対（たい）する反応（はんのう）は毎回（まいかい）同（おな）じになるとは限（かぎ）らず、状況（じょうきょう）によって変（か）わることがあります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「際（さい）に」と「時（とき）に」は、どちらも同（おな）じように使（つか）える場合（ばあい）もありますが、常（つね）に変（か）わらない状況（じょうきょう）や毎回（まいかい）同（おな）じように起（お）こる物事（ものごと）には「際（さい）に」を使（つか）うと不自然（ふしぜん）に聞（き）こえます。
attributes.body:
際（さい） is a noun in Japanese that means 'verge'. This is as in 'to be on the verge', and translates mostly as 'on the occasion of (A)', 'at the time of (A)', 'in case of (A)', or 'when (A)'. In the same way as 'verge' in English, it implies a fairly big or somehow important event, and will not be used with standard occurrences.

際（さい）に will appear after verbs in either their dictionary or past-tense forms, and after nouns. In the case of nouns, it will be preceded by の.

While (A) is likely to be a temporary or one-off event, 際（さい）に is not limited to one-off situations. It may also appear with regularly occurring events, but the way of reacting to that event may change depending on some one-off circumstances.

Caution

Although 際（さい）に and 時（とき）に may overlap in certain situations, 際（さい）に will sound unnatural when the situation involves something that typically does not change, or always happens the same way.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar
A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns

attributes.description: 際に and に際して

attributes.body: Both mean at the time of, but differ in nuance. 際に is a formal variant of 時に and applies broadly to past or present, as in 出発の際に写真を撮った (We took a photo at the time of departure). に際して is more formal, limited to present or future occasions, and highlights the special or official nature of the event, as in 契約に際して署名が必要だ (A signature is required at the time of signing a contract).

attributes.body: Both とき and 際に express the time of an action or event, but with different nuances and levels of formality. とき is common in everyday conversation and broadly used, like the English 'when'. 際に is more formal and often appears in official contexts, such as instructions, advice, or warnings related to specific events.

attributes.body: Both ついでに and 際に refer to additional actions tied to another event, but differ in tone. ついでに is an everyday expression for when something is done while convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). 際に is more formal and emphasizes a particular occasion, e.g. '来日の際にご連絡ください' ('Please contact us when you come to Japan').

attributes.body: Both mark occasions, but differ in nuance. 折には emphasizes opportunity or timing, often with verbs of judgment or decision, as in 来日の折にはぜひお立ち寄りください (Please visit when you come to Japan). 際に is more neutral, simply indicating when or at the time of, without implying seizing an opportunity.
